message.content:
Looking at the white stick-figure character (the main player, crouched low in the lower portion of the gameplay area), here are the visible anatomy defects:

## 1) Arms

- **Attachment:** The upper arms attach extremely high on the torso, essentially at the level of the head/neck rather than at a defined shoulder. One arm appears to originate almost from the circle that represents the head, so the "shoulder" joint has drifted upward — a shoulder-dislocation look.
- **Elbows:** The elbow joints are hard to locate because the arm segments don't form a normal zigzag. The leading (right) arm extends down-forward toward the blade weapon and appears to bend **backward/hyperextended** — the forearm flexes in the wrong direction relative to the upper arm, past a straight line (>170°), like the elbow is folding outward instead of inward.
- **Broken arm:** The **rear (left) arm is the broken one** — it's splayed backward and upward behind the torso at an angle a human shoulder can't reach, with the forearm continuing the same line instead of bending at an elbow. It reads as a straight rod pivoting from the torso rather than a two-segment limb with a functional elbow.
- Both arms essentially behave as single straight sticks rotating freely around one point, with the elbow either missing or bending the wrong way.

## 2) Joint-limit violations

Yes, clearly:
- The rear arm rotates **past the human shoulder range** (looks ~180°, pointing up-backward behind the body — a dislocated-shoulder appearance).
- The front arm's elbow is flexed **beyond ~170°**, hyperextending backward rather than flexing forward — anatomically impossible.

## 3) Legs and knees

- The character is sunk **far too low**: the knees are bent so deeply that the hips sit barely above the feet, past a normal crouch into a "collapsed" squat where the thighs are nearly horizontal.
- The knee bend looks like **inverted suspension** — the knees appear to fold inward/backward (the shin angles forward while the thigh angles back), similar to a reversed shock absorber rather than a human knee flexing only backward. The legs compress as if a spring under the pelvis is absorbing downward motion, and it has collapsed beyond any natural limit.

## 4) Pelvis/hip height

The pelvis is extremely low — roughly **one leg-segment's length (or less) above the ground**, almost touching the rooftop platform. For a mid-action combat pose it should be much higher; the hips have effectively sunk to the ground plane, only a small gap between the hip joint and the feet.

## 5) Torso lean

The torso leans **excessively forward** — well past a natural combat crouch, angled maybe 45°+ toward the direction of movement, with the head circle pushed out ahead of the hips. This matches the user's complaint that the character "leans too much" when idle/stopped; the spine doesn't return upright, it stays pitched forward past balance.

## 6) Shadow

The shadow (the dark circle/ellipse on the platform below) is **detached and misplaced** — it sits noticeably below and behind the feet, off to the lower-left, not directly under the character's planted foot contact point. The feet themselves aren't clearly planted on the surface the shadow occupies, so the shadow reads as "sliding/shifting" — it doesn't track the pose or the actual foot contact, exactly matching the complaint that "the shadow shifts" and looks disconnected from the character.
